primary.title: The Capitularies of Charlemagne
primary.author: Charlemagne
primary.rationale: Official decrees and laws issued by Charlemagne, providing direct insight into his governance and policies.

primary.title: The Royal Frankish Annals (Annales regni Francorum)
primary.author: Various (contemporary chroniclers, often associated with the Carolingian court)
primary.rationale: Chronicles detailing events during Charlemagne's reign, offering contemporary perspectives on his actions and achievements. While not solely authored by him, they are primary accounts of his era.

primary.title: Letters of Charlemagne
primary.author: Charlemagne
primary.rationale: Personal and official correspondence that can reveal his thoughts, relationships, and administrative concerns.

secondary.title: Charlemagne: Father of Europe
secondary.author: David Levering Lewis
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and well-regarded biography that analyzes Charlemagne's impact on European history, politics, and culture.

secondary.title: The Carolingian Renaissance: Image and Symbol
secondary.author: Paul Dutton
secondary.rationale: Examines the cultural and intellectual revival associated with Charlemagne's reign, focusing on art, literature, and education.

secondary.title: Charlemagne: The Formation of Europe
secondary.author: Richard Hodges
secondary.rationale: A scholarly assessment of Charlemagne's reign and its lasting influence on the political and social landscape of early medieval Europe.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources attributed to Charlemagne are often collections of his decrees (capitularies) or letters. Contemporary annals provide crucial historical context. Secondary sources focus on modern scholarly interpretations of his reign and legacy.
